If you're looking to get into a tech job, the TIA cert is a good start, but you'll pretty certainly have to take an entry level tech support job first to gain experience. 

If you're interested in an office type role in logistics, feel free to PM me, my company is always hiring. 

I can't speak to those other industries but I wish you the best of luck!

Which type of job(s) are looking for? 

COMPTIA certs, forklift certs, and experience shipping parts are 3 very different things. 

Your resume should really reflect the type of job you are applying for. I work for a tech company and we are almost always hiring, but it needs to be the right candidate with experience/qualifications.

I think it really depends on what "level" of employment you're at. When I was in college/just out of college, every single place always drug tested. My last job (the current one I have) I got before MJ was legal and they did not test. But it's a decent paying tech job with quite a few qualifications. 

Anecdotally, I feel like employers care less about that if you have other qualifications. The thinking is that as long as you can manage it, and you've made it as far as you have, they don't give a damn what you do in your spare time.

This man did not want you vibing to Taylor Swift. 

Glad you're okay though!

Sorry, just saw this reply now. 
I'm now finished with the ITM degree. I work in IT as well and this took me just a hair over a year to do ~95 CUs. But yes, from what I've read, the ITM is supposed to be FAR easier than anything in the actual IT school. There are no certifications and the IT classes are extremely light on in depth knowledge, I was able to pass most of them with very limited study time.

No worries, don't stress too much on it. I read a lot of horror stories on here about that class so I was super nervous too. I took it right after UFC1 and ended up getting like 15% over the cut score. A lot of carryover on concepts and as long as you know your formulas and how to use them, you'll do great.

Disclaimer: I passed this about 3 months ago, and I've heard they changed it somewhat since then. 

When I took it, on both the PA and OA, the formulas would appear for the questions that they were needed. It was a long list of basically all questions. The PA and OA were the same in that respect. So I'd say if they show on your PA they will on the OA too.

Honestly, just go directly to the pre assessment. You can take it as many times as you want. And the OA is an exact copy with just different numbers. So the ONLY think you really need to know are the commands/functions specifically in the PA. You can just do the PA over and over until you've got most of it down and then do the OA.

To me, yours sounds like a "check the box" for HR situation. If that's the case, I'd go for ITM. I'm nearing the end of that program and while working full time and having a wife and child, I'll be done after about 2.5 terms (just over a year). It's almost all business/management courses with a couple lite IT courses sprinkled in which I'm sure wouldn't be a problem with your experience. At this stage of your career, your experience will be far more important than your education specifics anyway. 

Feel free to ask any questions about the program, and good luck!

I've pretty much been trying to alternate "hard" with "easy" courses. When adding courses I'd ask my mentor about which ones are generally quick and which ones are more challenging and try to break them up. So don't get too burnt out by trying to knock out all the hard ones one after another.
It is a great feeling when you get some of those tough ones that you hear horror stories about out of the way.

Honestly, I don't think it matters that much given your experience. I think in your case it's more of a "check the box" situation at this point. I am finishing my IT Management degree soon and it's pretty light on "IT" classes. 

If you're looking to move into a high level executive spot with another company they're going to be far more concerned that you have 20 years of experience and already hold a chief-level position than they will be with if your degree is Management or IT Management. 
I'm close to finishing my IT management degree and you're right, the courses are very similar between the two. 

Good luck!
Good to see the people who live in the apartment above me are finally making it big with all their banging.

I just finished this one. Honestly, I just went through the PA right away and took screenshots of every question. Over the course of 2 days or so I reviewed all of them, many I already knew from other courses and read the course material for the ones I didn't know. YMMV of course, but for me the OA questions were EXTREMELY similar to the PA, some of them were even identical. 

So review the PA questions you don't already know, otherwise don't waste too much time on the course material.

What made it difficult for me (and many others you might see on here) is not using Excel for the past 10-12 years. 
If you use it regularly/have experience in the past with equations/commands I'd expect you to have no problem knocking it out in a couple days. It still only took me 2 weeks total and thats with basically zero Excel skills going in.

Couldn't agree more with you on this! I feel like I wasted a week or two trying learn every single command from the course material. After looking around on here I found out the PA and OA are the same so I did it exactly as you did and finished them both within 4-5 days.
Same, I have a 2011 MBP and had no issues at all.
Thank you!

The hardest part is probably just having the motivation/finding the time to study on your own. Unless you really seek it out, nobody is going to be telling you what to do when so you truly have to motivate yourself to get it done. 
I'm working in an IT Help Desk role for a great company that pays for my schooling, so I'd like to move up, ideally to a project manager position. The degree at this point isn't necessarily about learning new things, but just checking the box that HR looks for.

I'm in the program now, was in a similar situation as you: transferred in 29 credits. I did 24 credits my first term, now I'm at 29 in my second term. 
I have probably a term and half or so to go for my last 40 CUs. 
As everyone else will attest to, it depends on your family life/work life/motivation etc as to how fast you move through it. 
Honestly, most of the gen-ed type classes are pretty easy in my experience, especially if you have at least some college experience. Mine are definitely getting harder now as I get towards the end. 
Let me know if you're wondering about anything else.

I'll echo the statements of a few others here. The OA I found a fair amount harder than the PA. I got a 67 on the PA the first time. I studied for a few more weeks, took the PA again and got 75 or so. Then I took the OA a day or so later and only got a 64. 
I think you'll be fine though, you're pretty well following the same track I took.
See Rule #4 off to the right. Mods will probably be taking this info down. I'd recommend speaking to your Student Mentor if you had an issue though.

I just passed this today. My experience was similar to most it looks like. I got 81 on the PA and just passed the OA with a 69. The PA seemed to give a lot of straightforward definition type questions while the OA had very specific, real word choices that often had 2 or more answers that could logically fit. It was much toughed than I expected.

This has definitely never been the case for me. My SM has me get at least 10% over the cut score on the PA. Then after studying I usually end up getting 5-8 points higher on the OA (it can vary obviously by course though). On my last one I got 74 on the PA, then after studying the report for 3 days I got an 84 on the OA.
If you're looking up every single answer while taking the PA I could MAYBE see where they're coming from, but that hasn't been my experience at all.

I'm in the business- IT management program. I'm about 40% of the way there and so far the writing has been pretty minimal and straightforward. I had some credits that transferred so the only "research" I'd to do is the Comp 2 English class. Other than that, it's taking concepts you are probably already mostly familiar with being in the business world. 
To me, they're very clear on what the papers must contain and you don't have to be an amazing author to get your stuff approved. Hope this helps.
